note: Durability of scheduled work across a backend restart. This is the sharpest structural difference available at L2: an Express app schedules with in-process setTimeout, so restarting the process silently discards every pending message, while a SpacetimeDB scheduled reducer is a row in the database and survives. Matching SpacetimeDB here requires the model to build a persistent job queue with recovery on boot, unprompted. Restarts are an ordinary event — every deploy is one — so losing scheduled work to a restart is a real defect, not a contrived one.

features.name: Scheduled Delivery Survives Restart

criteria.desc: A message scheduled before a backend restart is still listed as pending afterwards — the schedule is persisted, not held in process memory (the actor re-registers if the app dropped the session on reload, so this measures scheduling durability rather than session persistence, which invariant 103 scores separately) The scheduling panel is re-opened after the reload because several apps keep the pending list inside a collapsible panel that defaults to closed.
The scheduled message actually sends at its appointed time despite the restart. In-process timers are gone after a restart, so the message never arrives.

features.note: Scheduling window is 200s because a SpacetimeDB host restart takes appreciably longer than an Express process restart; a shorter window let the message send before the pending list could be checked, which looked like a failure but was the schedule working.
